+# QuickBooks allocation worksheets for an accounting agent
+
+Use the existing merchant accounting connection to take an issued buyer period
+through a complete worksheet return and a reviewed native QuickBooks draft.
+The worksheet preserves every allocation, original native unit, expense or credit
+direction, current accountant assignment, and selected company/chart. Its editable
+fields carry the operator's include/exclude decisions, exact home-currency
+valuation and account choices.
+
+This workflow uses the four native worksheet methods in
+[QBO_WORKSHEETS.md](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/workspace/QBO_WORKSHEETS.md)
+and the existing [platform client and saved CLI operation](ACCOUNTING-PLATFORMS-CLIENT.md).
+The journal, review, native posting, response and accountant-return records remain
+owned by the original accounting workspace. A worksheet create retains a DRAFT.
+The following journal review and any provider posting remain separate explicit
+operations in the [original QuickBooks workflow](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/merchant-settlement-accounting/workspace/QBO_WORKFLOW.md).
+
+## Start with the existing workspace and company
+
+For an issued buyer period, complete [buyer startup](ACCOUNTING_BUYER.md) and
+select its original accountant handoff. Use the same configured workspace alias
+and original QuickBooks company. A retained company/chart snapshot is sufficient
+for worksheet preparation; these worksheet tools do not fetch credentials,
+refresh company data, contact a merchant, post a journal or send a payment.
+
+Add named inputs to the existing accounting workspace's platformInputs map.
+Paths resolve relative to the private merchant configuration. This example is
+an addition inside that existing definition:
+
+~~~json
+{
+  "platformInputs": {
+    "qbo-company": "../accounting/company-source.json",
+    "worksheet-export": "../accounting/worksheet-export-input.json",
+    "worksheet-open": "../accounting/worksheet-open-input.json",
+    "worksheet-inspect": "../accounting/worksheet-inspect-input.json",
+    "worksheet-returned": "../accounting/returned-allocations.csv",
+    "worksheet-plan": "../accounting/worksheet-plan-input.json"
+  }
+}
+~~~
+
+Keep the existing aliases too; each source map supports up to 64 declared aliases.
+The agent sends aliases and hashes, not arbitrary filesystem paths or large CSV
+bodies. The operator retains these files on the existing host. A source edit
+requires another read and review. The host rejects a source whose exact bytes no
+longer match a pinned SHA256.
+
+Open the original workspace once. Read
+merchant_accounting_qbo_worksheet_status for its actual
+binding.workspaceId, binding.sourcesSha256, current revision and reopenRequired.
+If reopenRequired is true, close and reopen that same original workspace before
+using its source or reconciling a create. Keep the original retained request.
+
+The export JSON contains:
+
+| Field | Required meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| binding | The complete two-field workspace/source binding returned by worksheet_status |
+| id, createdAt | The operator's saved worksheet UUID and timestamp, selected before export |
+| handoffId | The original buyer accountant handoff |
+| expectedParentId | Its exact current accountant return UUID, or null |
+| environment | sandbox or production, matching the selected company workflow |
+| companySnapshot | The complete retained native snapshot, when not using companySource |
+| draft | valuationBasis and exactly one complete editable row for every original allocation |
+
+A complete draft row has rowId, decision, amount, debitAccountId,
+creditAccountId, valuationNote, reason and description. All these values are
+strings. Use pending for an undecided allocation; keep empty text fields as
+empty strings. An excluded row still remains in the worksheet.
+
+A tool call can instead supply companySource and its optional initial
+companySourceSha256. That source contains the same original CompanyInfo,
+Preferences and accounts input accepted by qbo_company_preview. Do not also
+embed a companySnapshot. The native normalizer and worksheet compiler validate
+the exact company data.
+
+## Export and keep the original base
+
+Read merchant_accounting_qbo_worksheet_export with workspace and source.
+The response carries the source pins, native binding, worksheet identity, row
+and account counts, and three complete file descriptors:
+
+| File | Contents |
+| --- | --- |
+| worksheet.json | The full sealed native worksheet record, including every original base decision |
+| allocations.csv | The full original worksheet CSV, including all protected source columns and the JOURNAL row |
+| account-reference.csv | The complete selected company account reference |
+
+Use view:rows or view:accounts with offset and limit to inspect all entries.
+Pages contain at most 200 items. The complete files never depend on collecting
+or reconstructing a summary. Each descriptor contains its exact byte count,
+SHA256 and original file selection.
+
+Download through merchant_accounting_file using the returned selection and
+expectedSha256. Keep every selector unchanged while following readId and
+offset. The existing file reader verifies the original source once and then
+serves a private immutable snapshot for that read. It releases the snapshot at
+EOF; release an unfinished read through merchant_accounting_file_release.
+The client does this automatically when an iterator ends early.
+
+The selection's kind is qbo-worksheet. It retains worksheetAction, the input,
+returned-file and company aliases with their applicable digests, the complete
+worksheet result digest and the filename. Use the returned selection exactly.
+The file source is revalidated when opening a new read; subsequent chunks use
+that read's retained original snapshot.
+
+After reloading or changing tools, use worksheet_open with a JSON input holding
+binding, the complete original worksheet record, companySnapshot or a separate
+companySource, and environment. It reproduces the unchanged base CSV. A changed
+accountant parent, buyer source or company requires a new worksheet exported
+from the actual current source. Preserve the old worksheet as its prior edition.
+
+## Inspect the returned CSV and resolve each field
+
+The returned CSV is a separate declared input. Keep its actual UTF-8 bytes,
+including any BOM. Only CSV parsing removes the BOM; the returned-file SHA256
+covers the original complete bytes.
+

# Buyer, QuickBooks and Xero customer operations

This customer interface uses the existing accounting workspace, original buyer startup, QuickBooks and Xero controllers, and the same MCP connection as the other merchant tools. It gives an operator a complete path from original source selection and preview through retained requests, response reconciliation, accountant returns and exact file delivery.

The platform adapter is described in [ACCOUNTING-PLATFORMS.md](ACCOUNTING-PLATFORMS.md). Host configuration and ordinary accounting operations remain in [ACCOUNTING.md](ACCOUNTING.md). Backup, pause, restore and reader ownership use [ACCOUNTING-MAINTENANCE-CLIENT.md](ACCOUNTING-MAINTENANCE-CLIENT.md).

## Installed entry points

Both installed commands dispatch to this same module:

~~~text
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms --help
starforge merchant-mcp platforms --help
~~~

JavaScript applications can import the connection, SDK and prepared-operation functions:

~~~js
import {
  createAccountingPlatformClient,
  connectAccountingPlatformClient,
  accountingPlatformOperation,
  accountingPlatformActions,
} from '@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/accounting-platforms';

import {
  prepareAccountingPlatformOperation,
  runAccountingPlatformOperation,
  downloadAccountingPlatformFile,
} from '@tokenjunkielabs/starforge-merchant/merchant/accounting-platforms/operations';
~~~

The SDK accepts an already initialized MCP caller, including the merchant's original stdio transport. The connected SDK and CLI use the original HTTP MCP endpoint. They keep native plan, context, capture, response, operation and return IDs; they do not create a second financial engine or job queue.

## Buyer-issued source startup and receiving

Choose `--platform buyer` for a host-declared accounting alias configured with `sourceMode: "buyer"`. Host setup is in [ACCOUNTING_BUYER.md](ACCOUNTING_BUYER.md). This mode consumes the original issued buyer period, allocations, credits and outstanding source records. The existing buyer workspace and accounting Store remain their respective owners.

| Native tool | CLI or SDK entry | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `merchant_accounting_buyer_source_preview` | `source`; `client.sourcePreview()` | Original declared file, native validation, exact source digest and paged review |
| `merchant_accounting_buyer_initialize` | `preview --action initialize` → existing `prepare` / `execute` | Explicit Store initialization with reviewed source, name and operator |
| `merchant_accounting_buyer_startup` | `startup` or `status`; `client.startup()` | Retained source, workspace binding and first-handoff identity |
| `merchant_accounting_buyer_prepare` | `retained-source`; `client.prepareSource()` | Exact retained source pages and current revision for a named handoff |
| `merchant_accounting_buyer_handoff` | `preview --action handoff` → existing `prepare` / `execute` | Original startup handoff and exact same-request recovery |

Buyer startup and retained-source reads reopen the configured native workspace when its host has not opened it yet. Opening retains the original Store lease and does not initialize a missing buyer directory. Only the native `ACCOUNTING_BUYER_INITIALIZATION_REQUIRED` response identifies an uninitialized source during initialize recovery; `ACCOUNTING_NOT_OPEN` is never treated as missing financial work. Source-file preview remains usable before initialization, and other native open errors remain actionable.

Set the endpoint and workspace variables to the original configured host. Replace `issued_period` with an actual `buyerSources` alias returned by `sources`.

~~~sh
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms actions --platform buyer
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms sources \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform buyer

starforge merchant-accounting-platforms source \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform buyer \
  --source issued_period --view summary
~~~

The review returns `sourceSha256`, original byte count, period, monetary dimensions, allocation counts and outstanding source counts. For subsequent pages pass that exact digest in `--sha256`. Views are `allocations`, `outstanding` and `captures`, with `--offset` and `--limit` (maximum 200). Native amounts and source context stay unchanged.

### Initialize the selected source

Create a private JSON argument file with the actual alias and responsible operator. These are example field values:

~~~json
{
  "source": "issued_period",
  "name": "Reviewed buyer period",
  "actor": "Named operator"
}
~~~

An optional `sourceSha256` pins an earlier review. The initialization preview reads the actual file, retains its returned digest and byte count, and builds the exact native command. It does not initialize a directory.

~~~sh
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms preview \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform buyer \
  --action initialize --request "$CASE_DIR/initialize-arguments.json" \
  --out "$CASE_DIR/initialize-preview.json"

starforge merchant-accounting-platforms prepare \
  --dir "$CASE_DIR/initialize-operation" \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform buyer \
  --preview "$CASE_DIR/initialize-preview.json"

starforge merchant-accounting-platforms execute --dir "$CASE_DIR/initialize-operation"
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms reconcile --dir "$CASE_DIR/initialize-operation"
~~~

This reuses the existing private `request.json` / `state.json`, lease, send checkpoints and request digest. Before sending, reconciliation looks for retained native startup. Only the explicit native `ACCOUNTING_BUYER_INITIALIZATION_REQUIRED` result means initialization is absent. A different source, name or operator is a conflict. A failed read, paused workspace or uncertain Store does not become an absent result.

After an accepted initialization or lost reply, the same operation reads the retained source identity; its former import file is not needed for that observation. The recovered result includes the original workspace binding and first-handoff UUID. Explicit execute sends the same retained command only when the original initialization is actually absent. Reconcile never initializes.

### Review and recover the first handoff

~~~sh
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms startup \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform buyer

starforge merchant-accounting-platforms retained-source \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform buyer \
  --sha256 "$ISSUED_SOURCE_SHA256" --view allocations --offset 0 --limit 200
~~~

Prepare a private handoff argument file with its intended `name` and `actor`. You may also provide the previously observed `handoffId`, `sourceSha256` and `revision`; the preview rejects any mismatch instead of changing that choice. Otherwise it reads those identities from current retained startup and source review.

~~~sh
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms preview \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform buyer \
  --action handoff --request "$CASE_DIR/handoff-arguments.json" \
  --out "$CASE_DIR/handoff-preview.json"

starforge merchant-accounting-platforms prepare \
  --dir "$CASE_DIR/handoff-operation" \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform buyer \
  --preview "$CASE_DIR/handoff-preview.json"

starforge merchant-accounting-platforms execute --dir "$CASE_DIR/handoff-operation"
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms reconcile --dir "$CASE_DIR/handoff-operation"
~~~

The first-handoff UUID comes from original Store startup. The operation also binds native workspace/source identity, exact issued bytes, named handoff and the original create-request digest. Recovery matches all these values against compact retained handoff metadata. It does not infer acceptance from a matching UUID alone or invoke accountant create during reconcile. Native accepted retries retain the same request before checking an older revision.

Use `--platform qbo` or `--platform xero` on this same configured alias for the existing company/context, valuation, plan, response and return workflow below. Both consume the handoff already retained by buyer startup. The [buyer QuickBooks workflow](ACCOUNTING_BUYER.md#continue-quickbooks-from-the-issued-buyer-handoff) describes its complete allocation decisions, exact home values, production source requirements and original buyer return. Provider actions remain explicit in the selected original controller.

### Complete original source and accountant files

Save this private selection JSON:

~~~json
{"kind":"buyer-source"}
~~~

Download with the digest returned by source review:

~~~sh
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms download \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform buyer \
  --selection "$CASE_DIR/buyer-source-selection.json" --sha256 "$ISSUED_SOURCE_SHA256" \
  --out "$CASE_DIR/original-issued-buyer-source.json"
~~~

The maintained file reader retains its native handle and selectors, verifies every offset and complete SHA-256, and releases unfinished reads on caller disconnect. Output is the unchanged issued JSON, including every source and allocation record; review pagination does not truncate it. For an accountant packet use `kind: "accountant"` with its actual `handoffId`, optional returned `revisionId` and native `file` descriptor, retaining that file's own SHA-256. QuickBooks and Xero files use their respective `--platform qbo` and `--platform xero` selectors.

The SDK traverses a complete source view through native pages:

~~~js
const client = await connectAccountingPlatformClient({
  url: process.env.ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL,
  workspace: process.env.ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE,
  platform: 'buyer',
});
try {
  const startup = await client.startup();
  for await (const page of client.sourcePages({
    sourceSha256: startup.source.sha256,
    view: 'allocations',
    limit: 200,
  })) {
    consumeOriginalRows(page.page.items);
  }
} finally {
  await client.disconnect();
}
~~~

For a pre-initialization source, provide its actual `source` alias to `sourcePages()`. The first page establishes the digest if none was supplied; later pages require the same digest, byte count and complete row count. An empty view still returns its original zero-count page.

Save the operation directories with the complete native project handoff. Encrypted workspace backup/receiving remains the maintained accounting workflow. A received runtime must include `accounting-platform-buyer-client.mjs`, the original buyer catalog and updated retained-file reader from this edition. A source-only download does not include that runtime or the operator's private operation directories.


## Select the actual workspace and inputs

The examples below use environment variables for an already configured endpoint and workspace. Set ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL to its HTTPS URL or loopback HTTP URL, ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE to the existing alias, and MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN through the host's normal credential setup. Only the token's environment-variable name is retained in a prepared operation.

~~~sh
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms sources \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform qbo

starforge merchant-accounting-platforms open \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform qbo

starforge merchant-accounting-platforms status \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform qbo
~~~

The original sources response lists each workspace's platformInputs aliases. Those aliases refer to original JSON files declared by the host. The operator supplies the alias and, where available, the retained SHA-256. Native previews resolve the original bytes and return their exact source digest. Large provider JSON, base64 payloads and accountant CSV remain on the host.

For Xero, the same response supplies platforms.xero.tenants entries with alias and tenantId. A context capture requires both the selected alias and expectedTenantId. The adapter rejects a host alias that now points to a different tenant. Native plan operations also bind the selected alias to the tenant already retained in the plan.

Use actions to see every current native input field and required field. It runs locally and needs no merchant connection:

~~~sh
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms actions --platform qbo
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms actions --platform xero
~~~

Read commands preserve the platform's actual view names and pagination. Pages use offset and limit, with a maximum of 200 entries. To read a particular result, retain its original ID and select the appropriate native view. Reconciliation searches the complete relevant response or return inventory, checking that its total and revision stay consistent across pages.

## One durable preview-to-result workflow

Every change starts from a preview. Native preview tools return the command and binding directly. For review, cancellation, operation, resume and context-capture choices that have no separate native preview tool, the customer client reads the original record and labels its review CLIENT_REVIEW_OF_ORIGINAL_NATIVE_RECORD. It retains the caller's exact arguments, original IDs and native digests. Neither preview path performs the requested mutation.

A preview can contain rows, issues and source metadata needed by the operator. Its command contains the exact small mutation arguments. Save the whole preview before preparing or sending it.

The following is a QuickBooks create example. The example alias must be replaced by an alias returned by the actual sources call. The host's original request JSON contains its own native ID, actor, createdAt, source selection and plan choices.

~~~json
{
  "source": "approved_qbo_plan"
}
~~~

Save that JSON as a private create-arguments.json file. Its parent directory must be private and its file mode must have no group or world permissions. Use a new operation directory and new preview filename:

~~~sh
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms preview \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform qbo \
  --action create --request "$CASE_DIR/create-arguments.json" \
  --out "$CASE_DIR/create-preview.json"

starforge merchant-accounting-platforms prepare \
  --dir "$CASE_DIR/create-operation" \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform qbo \
  --preview "$CASE_DIR/create-preview.json"

starforge merchant-accounting-platforms execute \
  --dir "$CASE_DIR/create-operation"

starforge merchant-accounting-platforms reconcile \
  --dir "$CASE_DIR/create-operation"
~~~

Preparation is local. It seals the exact endpoint, platform, workspace, token environment name, normalized command, binding and full preview into request.json. It writes and syncs the initial state.json before publishing an executable request. Reopening that directory accepts only the same complete preview and destination.

Execution first looks for the original native result. If the exact result already exists, it returns that result without submitting another request. Otherwise it records the send boundary, then sends the retained command. After a reply or an uncertain reply, it reconciles the original identity again. The returned submissionAttempted flag describes this invocation; previouslyAttempted reflects the retained operation history.

Reconcile does not create a new plan, context capture, response import, provider request or journal operation. It can complete the existing pending accountant return associated with the same retained QuickBooks response or Xero return intent. Before that original resume call, the CLI records the exact recovery command and increments recoveryAttempts. Submission and recovery therefore remain distinguishable.

Keep the whole operation directory, including request.json and state.json. Missing state is not reconstructed as a fresh operation: its earlier send history is needed to interpret an uncertain response. An operation whose request file was never published is not ready to execute.

### Revisions and changed source

Use the native revision returned by the selected record. The engine decides whether a mutation is valid at that revision; the customer does not overwrite a caller's revision, workspace, actor, source digest or tenant.

If a native revision or source check rejects an unsent change, inspect the original record and prepare the newly reviewed command in a new directory. Preserve the earlier directory and any original request IDs needed for reconciliation. Do not edit request.json to remove an error or reset its history.

A source alias is a locator, not an identity. The command's sourceSha256, original previewSha256 and native IDs are the retained identity. If the host file changes after preview, the native source check reports that change before the new command can proceed.

## QuickBooks: original journal and response workflow

The customer covers the original manual response-import workflow and configured native posting. The native QuickBooks plan retains its normalized company and accounts, original handoff and accountant rows, editable journal and review. Both paths retain the actual provider response bytes and original accountant-return result.

| Customer preview action | Read before preparing | Identity retained for reconciliation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| create | Native plan preview from source; optional companySource preview | Original plan ID, actor, createdAt and journal integrity digest |
| review | Original plan summary and journal digest | Plan ID, review request UUID and native request digest |
| cancel | Original plan and explicit unusedConfirmed choice | Plan ID, cancellation UUID and native request digest |
| response-save | Original plan, response source preview, realm and expected accountant parent | Plan ID, response UUID, exact source digest and reviewed result digest |
| response-resume | Original retained response selected by responseId | The same response and result digests; no replacement response |

Normal progression is DRAFT to REVIEWED and, when the original response supports it, BOOKED. Cancellation is the native CANCELLED state. The original journal-entry.json file is available for REVIEWED or BOOKED plans. Read plan files and rows before choosing the exact original export.

To prepare a review, use these fields from the current plan and your explicit review decision:

~~~json
{
  "planId": "ORIGINAL_PLAN_UUID",
  "revision": 17,
  "id": "NEW_RETAINED_REVIEW_UUID",
  "actor": "Operator name",
  "note": "Original journal and account mapping reviewed.",
  "planSha256": "ORIGINAL_JOURNAL_SHA256"
}
~~~

The ID and digest strings above are placeholders. Use valid UUIDs and the actual 64-character digest from the original record. The revision shown is illustrative; use the observed revision. The preview command is --action review, followed by the same prepare/execute/reconcile sequence.

Cancellation additionally requires note and unusedConfirmed:true. Those fields describe the operator's actual decision about the native plan. The client preserves them rather than inferring them from an absent provider response.

For response-save, the argument file selects:

- planId and source: the original plan and the host's original response JSON alias;
- id, name, actor and createdAt: the explicit retained response identity;
- realmId: the selected QuickBooks company realm;
- expectedParentId: the current original accountant-return parent UUID, or null when there is no parent.

The native preview supplies sourceSha256, previewSha256 and the current revision for the command. An exact repeated response UUID is reconciled against its original request, provider bytes and result digest. A different response under the same ID is an identity conflict.

Response statuses retain their native meanings:

| Status | Customer behavior |
| --- | --- |
| FAULT | Return the original fault and retained source; no successful accountant result is asserted. |
| PENDING | Reconcile may finish the original already saved accountant return through response-resume. |
| SAVED | Return the original response and linked accountant-return identity. |

Read retained responses or files directly:

~~~sh
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms plan \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform qbo \
  --plan-id "$QBO_PLAN_ID" --view responses --offset 0 --limit 200

starforge merchant-accounting-platforms plan \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform qbo \
  --plan-id "$QBO_PLAN_ID" --view files
~~~

### Configured native company and journal posting

The same QBO client can inspect the host's native connection, capture the actual company and account pages, preview a reviewed journal and retain its native posting. The host declares platforms.qbo using either its original realmId, environment and token environment name, or the reviewed OAuth company described below. Optional minorVersion remains part of the original connection identity. The SDK uses that host-owned connection for provider requests.

Use read --action connection, or SDK connection(), to inspect the current configured destination. Native company capture is read --action company-fetch or SDK companyFetch(args). Supply the actual realmId and environment, and choose summary, accounts or snapshot. The snapshot view includes the full original company and its sourceDocuments; the accounts view is paged. expectedCompanySha256 can pin a subsequent requested view to the same original company content. This capture performs native GET requests and does not create a journal.

Native posting has two customer preview actions:

| Action | Selection | Execution behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| post | Original reviewed plan, current revision, stable posting UUID, actor, ISO createdAt and expectedParentId | Native preview binds the company, original journal bytes and full posting intent before the first submission. |
| post-resume | Existing nativePost UUID, current revision, actor and original previewSha256 | Only explicit execute invokes the original native continuation; reconcile reads its retained outcome. |

Use post only for a journal with no retained native posting. Its native preview returns the original planSha256, exact journal requestSha256, previewSha256 and postId. Prepare and execute that returned preview through the same durable operation directory. The original controller retains the posting intent and request bytes before external dispatch.

After an uncertain response, select the existing nativePost from the original plan. Preview post-resume using that operation's exact ID and digest, then prepare a new directory for that explicit resume decision. Reconcile alone will return executionRequired:true when this original operation still needs the prepared provider continuation. It will not call resumePost, query QuickBooks or repeat a journal POST.

~~~sh
starforge merchant-accounting-platforms preview \
  --url "$ACCOUNTING_MCP_URL" --workspace "$ACCOUNTING_WORKSPACE" --platform qbo \
  --action post-resume --request "$CASE_DIR/native-resume-arguments.json" \
  --out "$CASE_DIR/native-resume-preview.json"

starforge merchant-accounting-platforms prepare \
  --dir "$CASE_DIR/native-resume-operation" \
~~~

The argument file contains planId, revision, id, actor and previewSha256 from the selected native posting and current operator decision. The native continuation first uses any retained response that can finish locally. When provider access remains necessary, the original controller keeps the same request UUID, reviewed request bytes, company, environment and request URL. It queries the original journal identity and retains native query/read/post attempts. An already observed journal is not silently replaced by another posting. The customer does not implement its own provider retry algorithm.

| Native posting state | Customer interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| PREPARED or RUNNING | Original intent is retained or its native call is running; inspect the same operation. |
| UNCERTAIN or RETRYABLE | Original outcome requires continued observation or an explicit native resume. Retained retryAt remains authoritative. |
| RECEIVED | Original provider source is retained; the native controller can finish its accountant-return linkage. |
| BOOKED | The original native posting is linked to its retained accountant return. |
| FAULT or CONFLICT | Inspect the original native response, attempt records and lastError before selecting a further native action. |

## Embed the original customer client

Use an existing initialized structured-result MCP caller:

~~~js
const client = createAccountingPlatformClient({
  workspace: selectedWorkspaceAlias,
  platform: 'qbo',
  call: existingMcpCall,
});

const preview = await client.preview('create', {
  source: selectedOriginalInputAlias,
});
const operation = accountingPlatformOperation(preview);

// The application's existing durable store retains the full preview and operation.
await originalApplicationStore.savePrepared({ preview, operation });

const before = await client.reconcile(operation);
if (!before.found) {
  await originalApplicationStore.markSending(operation);
  await client.command(operation);
}
const result = await client.reconcile(operation, {
  recover: true,
  onRecovery: command => originalApplicationStore.recordRecovery(operation, command),
});
await originalApplicationStore.saveNativeResult(operation, result);
await client.disconnect();
~~~

The store methods in this example belong to the receiving application; they are not additional SDK exports. For an existing HTTP destination, use prepareAccountingPlatformOperation and runAccountingPlatformOperation to get the provided private journal instead of implementing another send-history store. In particular, retain the CLI's no-repeat behavior for uncertain context captures.

Direct SDK command validates and sends the exact retained command. Reconcile checks its original returned identity. Applications should preserve both steps and retain the request before command; a successful transport reply by itself is not the reconciliation result.

SDK read accepts only declared native read actions. Mutation calls go through a validated preview/operation and command. Argument validation uses the adapter's original wire schemas. An explicitly supplied workspace that differs from the selected alias is rejected rather than silently replaced.

## Reader, operation and workspace lifetime

The client uses the same maintenance reader as accounting downloads. Complete downloads release their original read. Partial streams can be returned early and are released when their iterator closes. If the caller opens a retained read through its existing connection, registerFileRead/readId and releaseFile let it keep that reader under the same ownership.

disconnect drains only this caller's owned file reads and preserves the original workspace and provider operations. The client returns the operation IDs it observed from its own operate calls through retainedOperations; the same custody view includes original native QBO posts observed from post and post-resume calls. Those IDs remain addressable through the original native controllers after this caller disconnects.

close is an explicit workspace close. It drains the caller's work and invokes the existing workspace close path. The native controller owns cancellation, completion and retained operation state. Read the original controller state after reopening instead of assuming that ending a transport erased its jobs.

maintenanceCommand('pause', ...) drains admitted customer calls before the existing maintenance pause. After resume, use the same original source IDs and digests with a newly owned read. The original response, archive and platform bytes remain in their existing source custody.

## Output, errors and recovery state

The CLI writes machine-readable JSON. Error records preserve the native or customer code and, for a prepared operation, the original operationDirectory, platform and action.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | A local preparation, read, or exact observed result completed. |
| 3 | The original result is not observed yet, or its retained operation is still pending. |
| 2 | An error, native FAULT, FAILED or INTERRUPTED outcome requires inspection. |

The returned native object is preserved with found, pending, submissionAttempted, previouslyAttempted and recoveryAttempted. An uncertain reply stays in the private state record even when a later lookup finds the original result.

Use the existing operation directory for later reconciliation. Retain its original request, source files and native IDs when moving machines or reopening a session. Keep the same configured endpoint, workspace and token environment name; resolving a missing reply does not justify selecting another company or tenant.

This guide describes the implemented customer protocol. Native provider results and release acceptance belong to the original platform operation and its retained result; examples and previews do not assert a live provider transaction.

~~~js
  configPath: '/srv/merchant-config/merchant-mcp.json',
~~~

The environment passed to startMerchantMcp supplies the host's OAuth directory and
secret references as well as its existing transport authentication. Direct
openMerchantOperator callers can supply the same environment through
options.accounting.environment. Native embedded operation hosts can pass the
original OAuth runtime options through options.accounting.quickbooksOAuth;
these are trusted host options, not merchant JSON or customer tool arguments.

## One lifetime and one delivery path

Open the workspace with merchant_accounting_open. Its operating maintenance
controller opens the original accounting store and constructs the accountant,
QuickBooks and Xero controllers under that same lease. QuickBooks recovers
retained PENDING response/accountant intents and completes an already received
native posting from its retained local files. Both native controllers preserve
interrupted provider-operation state for the original reviewed continuation.

Pause and close use the existing maintenance workflow. They stop new admission,
drain accepted calls and file reads, then close both controllers' owned native tasks before
closing the original accounting workspace. Resume constructs the original
controllers against those same directories and identities.

A customer disconnect releases only that customer's retained file reads.
Explicit workspace close is the owner operation. The customer guide distinguishes
those actions and keeps original native operations available for reconciling an
uncertain client response.

## QuickBooks: connected company to the original accountant return

1. Open merchant_accounting_qbo_status and page handoffs/plans. Read the selected
   handoff with merchant_accounting_qbo_handoff. The row view preserves original
   native amounts, source classifications, frozen adjustment context and the
   current accountant parent.

2. Read merchant_accounting_qbo_connection to check the host's exact company,
   environment and credential availability. merchant_accounting_qbo_company_fetch
   performs the original native CompanyInfo, Preferences and complete Account
   query, including inactive accounts. Default output is a compact summary;
   accounts view pages the captured chart and snapshot view returns the full
   validated company with its original sourceDocuments. Each fetch is a fresh
   native read. Carry expectedCompanySha256 when comparing another page so a
   changed company/chart is reported instead of silently mixing captures.

3. The operator retains that company snapshot inside the declared journal input,
   or writes the original sourceDocuments into the existing qbo-company import
   format. merchant_accounting_qbo_company_preview reads that host-selected source
   and displays actual account identity, currency, activity, type and eligibility.
   Use the same companySource in journal preview when the request does not already
   contain its companySnapshot. The full native source is available to the SDK;
   tool arguments continue to carry the host alias and exact source hash.

4. Call merchant_accounting_qbo_preview with the declared journal source and
   optional companySource. Review the actual home-currency values, balanced native
   lines, selected accounts and original source context. Retain and execute its
   exact merchant_accounting_qbo_create command. The native preview digest and
   source pins identify the original DRAFT plan; the same exact request reopens
   that UUID.

5. Read merchant_accounting_qbo_plan and send merchant_accounting_qbo_review with
   its current revision, stable review UUID, actor, note and planSha256. The original
   controller reserves the selected company/events and exposes journal-entry.json.

6. Call merchant_accounting_qbo_post_preview for that reviewed plan with the current
   revision and expectedParentId plus a stable posting id, actor and createdAt.
   The native preview selects the configured company and exact retained journal
   bytes. Retain its complete command and binding, then explicitly execute
   merchant_accounting_qbo_post. The original controller publishes its immutable
   intent/request, records native attempts, reconciles the exact original journal
   and links the same accountant return.

7. After a lost reply, read that plan's nativePost before attempting another
   operation. The SDK's reconcile reads the saved native identity. An explicit
   merchant_accounting_qbo_post_resume selects the same id and previewSha256
   with the current workspace revision and resuming actor. The original native
   controller may query/read the provider and, when its retained operation permits,
   submit the original request. Customer reconciliation does not automatically
   invoke this execution action.

8. When nativePost is BOOKED, its responseId/journalEntryId and original accountant
   return remain attached to the same plan. Retrieve intent.json/request.json with
   nativePost:true; retrieve a native attempt's response.json/receipt.json with
   its attemptId. Plan view native-attempts pages the complete original history,
   and view files supplies the exact selectors for all retained files.

The native preview exposes three distinct digests. Keep each in its original role:

| Field | Native meaning |
| --- | --- |
| planSha256 | The retained reviewed QuickBooks plan |
| requestSha256 | Exact original journal-entry.json bytes sent to the provider |
| previewSha256 | The native posting intent, including its UUID/time, actor, company, request URL, parent and request/plan hashes |

The native posting remains the original controller's operation:

| Native status | Customer operation |
| --- | --- |
| PREPARED or RUNNING | Observe the original retained operation; allow its owner to finish |
| UNCERTAIN or RETRYABLE | Inspect retained attempts and retryAt, then explicitly continue the same reviewed posting when appropriate |
| RECEIVED | The original provider response is retained; continue its local accountant import using the native operation |
| BOOKED | Retrieve and reconcile the original journal and accountant return |
| FAULT or CONFLICT | Inspect the exact retained native response and reconcile the company's original records before another reviewed action |

The native controller applies its provider throttle and Retry-After handling.
Neither a customer timeout nor a missing transport reply creates a new posting
UUID. Once the original native journal has been observed, its retained identity
continues to govern recovery.

### Import an existing native posting response

A previously received provider JournalEntry or Fault can use the original saved
response workflow on the reviewed plan:

1. Select its exact original JSON through the declared response source. Call
   merchant_accounting_qbo_response_preview with the stable response UUID, name,
   actor, createdAt, realm and current expectedParentId.

2. Review and execute the returned merchant_accounting_qbo_response_save command.
   The original controller retains the response and return intent, applies the
   accountant import and links its saved return. PENDING becomes SAVED and the
   plan becomes BOOKED when that original return is linked.

3. For an interrupted response, read its full paged history.
   merchant_accounting_qbo_response_resume continues the same planId/responseId
   with the current revision and actor. It operates the retained original return.

A native Fault remains a retained FAULT response. Cancellation of an unused
journal uses merchant_accounting_qbo_cancel with a stable cancellation UUID,
the original plan digest, reason and unusedConfirmed:true. Retained native
posting attempts and matched pending/saved returns remain subject to the
original controller's cancellation rules.

## Reconcile the original identities

The customer CLI stores the accepted command and its binding before dispatch.
After an uncertain reply, it observes the original native record. It does not
infer absence from a transport error or silently create another operation UUID.

| Operation | Original identity to reconcile | Native record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| QuickBooks draft | Plan UUID and native preview/plan digest | qbo_plan record.integrity |
| QuickBooks review | Plan UUID and original review UUID | record.review |
| QuickBooks cancellation | Plan UUID and original cancellation UUID | record.cancellation |
| QuickBooks native posting | Plan UUID, native posting UUID and original preview, plan and request SHA256 | qbo_plan record.nativePost; observe the original status, then explicitly execute post-resume only when continuation is needed |
| QuickBooks response | Plan UUID and original response UUID, byte/result hashes | qbo_plan view:responses |
| QuickBooks resume | Same response UUID | Original PENDING/SAVED response and linked return |
| Xero context import/capture | Original context UUID and import/tenant identity | xero_context record |
| Xero plan | Plan UUID, planSha256 and original normalized request hash | xero_plan record |
| Xero draft/refresh operation | Plan UUID and original operation UUID/request hash | xero_operation |
| Xero response import | Plan UUID and original capture UUID/source request hash | xero_plan view:captures and xero_comparison |
| Xero accountant application | Plan UUID, original return UUID/capture/preview hash | xero_plan view:returnIntents and view:returns |
| Xero retained-return resume | Same retained return intent | Original PREPARED/APPLIED intent and linked return |

Status and plan tools provide total/offset/limit/items for complete paging.
Ordinary summary lists are recent selections, not a complete absence check.
Retained operations may apply or link an already saved result during recovery;
that action keeps its original identity and uses the original engine.

The original missing-record codes are QBO_PLAN_NOT_FOUND,
QBO_RESPONSE_NOT_FOUND, XERO_CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND, XERO_PLAN_NOT_FOUND,
XERO_CAPTURE_NOT_FOUND and XERO_OPERATION_NOT_FOUND. Other failures retain their
actual meaning. A source mismatch or native accounting conflict requires
reconciling the original request and current state.

# Buyer-only accounting through the configured MCP host

A host can now declare the original accountant as a buyer-only workspace. The
same accounting provider retains an issued buyer period, its expense and credit
allocations, the first accountant handoff, returned bookkeeping references and
the original QuickBooks, Xero and encrypted-recovery histories. The input is the native
`stellar-forge.buyer-accountant-source.v1` document produced by the buyer expense
workspace; its validator remains the authority for the exact accepted schema.

## Declare the original source

Use `sourceMode:"buyer"` on the existing accounting workspace declaration. The
workspace directory may be new or an already initialized original buyer-only
accountant. Paths resolve relative to the host's configuration file.

```json
{
  "workspaces": {
    "expenses": {
      "label": "Buyer expense accounting",
      "sourceMode": "buyer",
      "directory": "./buyer-accounting",
      "buyerSources": {
        "issued-period": "../issued/period-accountant-source.json"
      },
      "accountantReturns": {
        "reviewed-return": "../accountant/returned.csv"
      },
      "platformInputs": {
        "qbo-company": "../accountant/original-qbo-company.json",
        "qbo-plan": "../accountant/reviewed-qbo-buyer-plan.json",
        "qbo-response": "../accountant/original-qbo-response.json",
        "qbo-chart-change": "../accountant/reviewed-qbo-chart-change.json",
        "xero-context": "../accountant/original-xero-context-request.json",
        "xero-plan": "../accountant/reviewed-xero-plan.json",
        "xero-response": "../accountant/original-xero-response-request.json"
      },
      "recovery": {
        "stateRoot": ".",
        "backupRoot": "../accounting-backups",
        "passEnv": "STARFORGE_ACCOUNTING_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Declare only the aliases whose original files are actually available. Empty maps
may be omitted. Keep the state and source directories private (0700) and the
issued file private (0600). The original startup reader accepts a regular,
owner-controlled source up to 64 MiB, checks its exact bytes while reading, and
validates the native issued period and aggregate allocations.

This standalone declaration is accepted by the existing initializer:

```sh
starforge merchant-mcp init-accounting --dir /absolute/private/accounting-operator --accounting /absolute/private/accounting.json
starforge merchant-mcp serve --config /absolute/private/accounting-operator/merchant-mcp.json
```

The ordinary host still uses its configured loopback listener and bearer
credential. Existing stdio and configured-provider clients expose the same
registered accounting tools. Configuring the provider does not initialize the
accounting directory, import a source, contact a bookkeeping service or make a
payment.

An existing merchant configuration can instead include the declaration under
`accounting`; preserve its other provider settings. An omitted sourceMode keeps
the existing merchant contract, including its required outbox, proof and terms
paths. A buyer declaration omits those paths and merchant-only input maps. Its
supported accounting operations are source startup, accountant handoff/returns,
QuickBooks, Xero, chart changes, exact retained files and native operating recovery. The host reports these
capabilities with each alias. Merchant sales, collection, statements, Bitwave,
Cryptoworth and runbook operations continue under their original merchant alias.

## Preview and explicitly initialize

1. Call `merchant_accounting_sources` and select the declared buyer alias.
2. Call `merchant_accounting_buyer_source_preview` with `workspace` and
   `source`. It reads the original private file without opening a workspace.
3. Keep its returned `sourceSha256`. Review the original period, source context,
   exact native totals, credits and outstanding reservations.
4. To read the complete source review, use `view:"allocations"`,
   `"outstanding"` or `"captures"`, with `offset` and `limit` (up to 200).
   Supply the same sourceSha256 on every subsequent page. A changed original
   file rejects that old selection.
5. Submit `merchant_accounting_buyer_initialize` with the same alias and digest,
   plus the actual source name and operator.

Example tool arguments, with the digest copied from that actual preview:

```json
{
  "workspace": "expenses",
  "source": "issued-period",
  "sourceSha256": "<exact SHA256 returned by source_preview>",
  "name": "Reviewed issued expense period",
  "actor": "<operator name>"
}
```

Initialization uses the original Store lease and startup writer. It retains the
complete issued bytes in the accountant's private inputs, source context and
summary, original initialization name/operator, and the native first-handoff
UUID. Its result includes the actual workspace/source binding and that startup
record. The response keeps the original workspace ID and source-binding digest;
host-owned input paths are omitted from the buyer projection. Original source
values and reviewed request text remain unchanged. The configured accounting
session then opens normally, or remains in
the explicitly declared paused-recovery mode.

After an uncertain response, repeat the identical initialization arguments.
An accepted initialization recovers from its retained original source without
rereading the former import file. Changing the source digest, name or operator
does not silently replace that retained initialization. The source alias remains
a host declaration; recovery does not allow arbitrary file paths.

Once initialized, `merchant_accounting_open` reopens the retained directory.
It reads the original source binding and the Store rechecks it under the writer
lease. Reopening does not require the former import path or a new source alias.
The host cannot reinterpret a merchant directory as a buyer directory.

## Prepare and recover the first handoff

Call `merchant_accounting_buyer_startup` after opening. It returns the original
binding, current workspace revision, source identity and first-handoff UUID.
Then call `merchant_accounting_buyer_prepare` with the retained sourceSha256.
This reads the retained issued file and supports the same complete paged review
as the pre-initialization preview.

Use `merchant_accounting_buyer_handoff` with:

| Field | Original value to retain |
| --- | --- |
| workspace | The configured buyer alias. |
| handoffId | The native startup UUID returned by prepare. |
| sourceSha256 | The retained original issued-source digest. |
| revision | The current workspace revision shown by prepare. |
| name | The reviewer's handoff name. |
| actor | The named reviewer. |

Save that full request before submission. The original accountant writer uses
the same startup ID and request identity on every retry. If it accepted the
handoff but the reply was lost, the identical request recovers its original
record before checking the now-old workspace revision. A different name,
operator or source under that same ID remains a request conflict.

The existing `merchant_accounting_accountant`,
`merchant_accounting_accountant_rows`,
`merchant_accounting_accountant_preview` and
`merchant_accounting_accountant_apply` tools inspect and review the original
handoff and its returned editions. The existing
`merchant_accounting_accountant_buyer_prepare/create` path remains available
for an explicitly selected additional issued source; it does not replace the
startup's retained source or first-handoff identity.

## Read exact original files

Use the existing retained file reader with `kind:"buyer-source"` to retrieve the

`kind:"qbo"` and `kind:"xero"` select the original native plan and response files.

## Continue QuickBooks from the issued buyer handoff

Use `--platform qbo` on this same buyer alias after the original handoff is
retained. The session opens its original QuickBooks and Xero controllers over
the same accountant owner. A host may use imported native company/response files
or configure its existing QuickBooks company through `platforms.qbo`. The
[platform connection guide](ACCOUNTING-PLATFORMS.md) covers both the original
token-environment connection and a reviewed OAuth company selection. The saved
realm, environment, company snapshot and token scope retain that connection's
existing contract.

Read the original handoff with `read --action handoff`, supplying its actual
`handoffId` in the private request JSON. Select `view:"rows"` and page the
complete allocation inventory. Every row retains its expense or returned-credit
kind, original source/economic identities, native amount, recognition date,
cost-center/project coding, source observation and current accountant assignment.

Prepare a `platformInputs` file with the original QuickBooks request fields:
its stable `id`, `createdAt`, `name`, `actor`, `handoffId`,
`expectedParentId`, actual company/realm/base currency/environment, `txnDate`,
optional `docNumber`, `valuationBasis` and `rows`. The native handoff supplies
the current parent and source rows; preserve those observed identities.
For **every** allocation, supply one explicit decision:

- An included row has its original `rowId`, `decision:"include"`, an exact
  positive two-decimal home-currency `amount`, `valuationNote`, and the
  accountant's chosen `debitAccount` and `creditAccount`. These accounts use
  the actual native Account.Id values in their `value` fields.
- An excluded row has its original `rowId`, `decision:"exclude"` and a specific
  `reason`. Its original accountant fields remain unchanged. Zero-native
  allocations and previously booked/excluded allocations require this decision.

Include between 1 and 500 allocations in a journal and retain a decision for
every other issued allocation. State the valuation source and tax treatment in

the compiler performs no exchange-rate selection or automatic tax calculation.

matched transfer and observation digest. The existing sandbox path retains
development source as development.

## Continue the existing Xero operation

The same buyer session retains its original Xero controller and accountant
instance. Original source, context, plan, operation, response, comparison and
return APIs keep their existing contract.

A zero-native allocation cannot acquire an unrelated positive fiat valuation;
the original Xero decision path retains an explicit exclusion where required.
Unknown prices and currencies retain their original meaning. A provider's draft

native amount, development/testnet scope and buyer-return acceptance.

## Pause, back up, receive and reopen the same operation

The existing `merchant_accounting_maintenance_*` tools retain the whole native
buyer accountant using its declared state root and separate backup catalog.
Use the original sequence: pause, review, acknowledge stopped external writers,
capture the encrypted backup, verify the exact selected backup, restore its
original destination, then resume. Keep each native request ID, review identity
and archive digest. The passphrase stays in its host environment variable.

The backup includes the original startup source and binding, native workspace
history, first handoff, QuickBooks plans/responses, Xero contexts/plans/responses,
chart-change reviews/applications, returned editions and source files under the
original recovery rules. An incomplete restore retains
the same native marker; resume that authenticated original backup rather than
initializing over it.

Close the MCP alias before opening the same directory in the original
accountant browser, buyer CLI or managed Applications. All use the existing
exclusive writer lease. Close drains accepted calls and verified readers.
Provider-wide close also finishes any already accepted source previews.
